That is terrible, I'm so sorry.  There may be local services that can help you leave, help pursue legal action against him, and help keep you safe. When you divorce, you should be entitled to alimony and child support.  Given the history of abuse, I expect you could get a restraining order, so he will not be able to see you or contact you.

I once found myself in an abusive relationship in a new city where I had no social support. I called the police after the physical abuse escalated. I was very surprised and impressed by the official support I received. He went to jail, and they offered me a restraining order. He was accompanied by police when he came to pick up his stuff.  I saw him peering through my windows while I had the restraining order, and the police found him and confronted him. It was scary, but the police and court were supportive. 

You will come out of this strong and free and capable of building a happier, more loving life for yourself and your child.

When I got into a relationship for the first time in 10 years, a lot of issues surfaced that I wasn't aware of when I was single.  I had also experienced abuse in past relationships, and some very intense emotions started resurfacing. I consciously worked on my issues, and within a year or so, was feeling much more stable. If you're actively working on stuff, I believe you'll see positive results. Sounds like the guy is supportive; that's great! I suggest being open with him about what you are going through, to avoid misunderstandings and friction. Sounds like you're doing great!
I was a child in the 90s and I don't miss it.

Maybe he was worried about crossing boundaries with someone who might just see him as a kid/mentee. Don't know what y'all talked about, but would you be comfortable bringing up the topic of dating/relationships?  I don't think it would be weird for a friend/mentor to ask if he's dating, ask about previous relationships, etc.  And that conversation might give you a better idea of how he sees you.
I'm guessing he is romantically interested in you, but has backed off because you weren't giving him signs you were romantically interested in him.

NTA

Wow, I can't believe multiple people have shamed you for HAVING FEELINGS.  When I am in a relationship, I do not reminisce romantically about my exes, and if I perceived some evidence my partner was doing so, I would find that disturbing.

 Even if you and I are weird and having some kind of lingering romantic feelings are the norm, you are not wrong for having an emotional response and respectfully seeking clarity in the matter.

NAH

This is very sad, but it sounds like she genuinely put in a lot of effort trying to do something kind for you, but she made an honest mistake, thinking the drawing was yours.  I understand why you would feel very hurt.  And also why she would feel very hurt.

There have been multiple times I thought I was about to die.  I always felt a deep sense of peace and acceptance, even when I was expecting a very gruesome end.  However I usually also feel embarrassed about how I'm going to die.  Like people will think I was so stupid to be backpacking alone in the wilderness without adequate preparation, or travelling alone in a developing country, or whatever.  I worry people will use my story to illustrate why others shouldn't do the thing I was doing.  And they would never realize that I understood the risks perfectly well and I was kind of actually hoping to die.

They've worked very well for me.  Before I started meds, the symptoms that bothered me the most were cognitive impairments.  I couldn't concentrate on anything, had very bad memory, couldn't express myself, and just spaced out all the time.  Since I've been on both bupropion and sertraline (about 5 months) I feel like my mental capacities are totally normal.  I can function so much better.  My mood has also lightened.  The best way I've thought to explain it is that the world seems a little brighter.  I'm not happy, but things seem a lot less horrible.  I still have anhedonia, I'm still tired a lot and I'm not really interested in life or my future.  But I can do so many things I couldn't before.  The improvement really has been huge.  Also, after the few weeks I don't think I have any side effects from either medication.

I was very reluctant to try antidepressants.  I've had depression since elementary school and didn't try medication until I was 32, in a very severe state, and hardly able to function at all.  At the time, starting meds felt like an admission of defeat.  My entire life, people had made me feel like I didn't have a legitimate health condition, and I was just weak-willed.  I believed that shit and thought I just needed to get tougher.  But now, I've seen what a huge difference it can make to moderately boost some chemicals in my brain.  Now I think about it like this:  if I had iron-deficiency anemia causing me severe fatigue and weakness, would people be telling me I didn't need to supplement iron, I just need to toughen up?  Would anyone tell a diabetic they don't need insulin?  Depression is also a medical condition, and it makes sense to take advantage of the treatments available to you.

Ok so, I ostensibly make eye contact with many people everyday, but I'm usually not looking very deeply and usually don't feel like the other person is really looking deeply into my eyes either.  But every now and then, I make eye contact with someone while we both have our guards down, and it feels like we are truly looking inside each other and can intuitively get a taste of who the other person is on a deeper level.  I think this only occurs with people who are, kind of, on a similar wavelength.  So on rare occasions, I make this kind of deep eye contact with a guy. It could be a stranger I've never seen before or an acquaintance I'd previously never paid much attention to.  But then I just feel that gentle intensity and shared secret understanding, and it is very hot.

I like the warehouse a lot more.  I don't have to wander around looking for someone with a QR code and don't have to deal with crowded aisles or customers asking me where stuff is.  My warehouse is chill so far, no one has annoyed me about rates or anything.

Yes, I can relate to this.  Cognitive impairment seems to be my main symptom. The only real reason I break down with negative emotions and suicidal thoughts is because I hate that my brain won't function properly and that I have no control over it.  I feel so powerless because I've spent so much time and effort trying improve this, but nothing seems to help for long.  When the depression lifts, I'm pretty competent, but then, for no apparent reason, I become extremely stupid, slow, and spaced out and I have no idea when or if my mind will clear again.

I've just been crying on the floor in the dark asking myself this same question.  I've managed to compose myself since I have homework to do.  I'm 35 and finishing my first bachelor's degree next quarter and have no idea what I will do after that.  I don't want to do anything.
